text:
Devin: heads up — seeing a small spike in 5xxs from APAC customers over the last hour, root cause looks IPv6-only paths failing after about ~1200B responses.
Maya: hmm, APAC historically hits NAT64 gateways for some mobile carriers. any logs from the edge?
Devin: yes — edgelb shows client <-> backend handshake succeeded, but then we see TCP RSTs and some ICMPv6 'packet too big' messages.
Lee: that screams MTU/fragmentation. Are we sending large chunked SSE responses?
Devin: streaming tokens, sometimes >1400 bytes in a single TCP segment. curl -6 replicates locally: `curl -6 -v https://api.redwood.test/stream` then connection drops after first chunk.
Sam: can you dig up a `tcpdump` or similar? Need to confirm if path MTU discovery is failing (no ICMPv6 allow).
Devin: attached snippet from tcpdump (abbreviated):
```
14:23:01.123 IP6 fe80::1 > 2001:db8::1: TCP 54321 > 443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1432, ack 1, win 65535
14:23:01.124 IP6 2001:db8::1 > fe80::1: ICMP6 Packet too big, mtu=1280
14:23:01.125 IP6 fe80::1 > 2001:db8::1: TCP 54321 > 443: Flags [R], seq 1432, win 0
```
Maya: okay that ICMP6 is expected if responder wants smaller MTU. Are our edge NLBs dropping ICMPv6 or rewriting?
ops-bot: infra-note: edgelb v2.4.1 introduced a UDP offload that can drop ICMPv6 when hardware path MTU is enforced. Ticket INF-8243 open.
Ana: INF-8243 — nice. Does it affect all regions or only APAC?
ops-bot: current telemetry shows failures concentrated in apac-1 and apac-2 where our partners use carrier-grade NAT64 with small MTU (1280).
Lee: so client prefers IPv6 (AAAA present), then NAT64 translates, but ICMPv6 'Packet too big' from translator back to client doesn't make it to our backend -> PATH MTU stuck -> connection resets.
Sam: possible mitigations: 1) enable TCP MSS clamping on the LB so backend never sends >1280, 2) drop AAAA for affected front domains in APAC, 3) force IPv4 egress for streaming routes.
Maya: MSS clamp seems low-risk. Can we apply at edge for apac-1/2 only?
Devin: quick test: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1220` helped in a canary host.
Ana: good proof. What's the perf tradeoff? smaller MSS increases packets, but token throughput little changed. Cost impact negligible.
Lee: could also tweak our response chunking to break big frames under 1200 bytes as a software workaround while infra change rolls out.
Sam: agree — do both: short-term app-level chunking + MSS clamp at LB as long-term fix. We should avoid removing AAAA unless we have to.
Maya: rolling plan?
Devin: propose: 1) roll MSS clamp on apac-1 for a single canary subnet now, 2) enable chunk-size limit on streaming service for canary customer group, 3) monitor 1h for errors and latency, 4) if stable, roll to apac-2, then global.
Ana: +1. who will own the LB change?
Lee: I can push the change to the edgelb config and coordinate with infra on INF-8243.
ops-bot: change-request created: CR-3912 by Lee (MSS clamp apac-1 canary). Scheduled immediate.
Devin: doing canary test now. will post results in 20m.
Maya: also add a short FAQ for support — customers asking why AAAA works but streams drop. mention NAT64 and MTU.
Sam: FYI: if carriers rewrite ICMP or drop it entirely, MSS clamp + smaller chunks is the only workable path.
Devin: can confirm canary succeeded — errors dropped to baseline, chunking workaround didn't increase tail latency much.
Ana: awesome. after full roll, let's follow up with a postmortem note linking to INF-8243 and CR-3912 so sales/support can reference it.
Lee: will open a doc in /confluence and assign follow-up items.
Devin: thanks all :thumbsup:
Maya: nice catch — great cross-team response.
